setup: as hr_install.sql does, as SYSTEM in FREEPDB1: CREATE USER HR … QUOTA UNLIMITED ON users; GRANT CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW, CREATE PROCEDURE, CREATE SEQUENCE, CREATE SESSION, CREATE SYNONYM, CREATE TABLE, CREATE TRIGGER, CREATE TYPE, CREATE VIEW TO HR; ALTER SESSION SET CURRENT_SCHEMA=HR (NLS American); then @hr_create.sql

tables.name: COUNTRIES
tables.comment: country table. References with locations table.

columns.name: COUNTRY_ID
columns.comment: Primary key of countries table.

columns.name: COUNTRY_NAME
columns.comment: Country name

columns.name: REGION_ID
columns.comment: Region ID for the country. Foreign key to region_id column in the departments table.

tables.name: DEPARTMENTS
tables.comment:
Departments table that shows details of departments where employees
work. references with locations, employees, and job_history tables.

columns.name: DEPARTMENT_ID
columns.comment: Primary key column of departments table.

columns.name: DEPARTMENT_NAME
columns.comment:
A not null column that shows name of a department. Administration,
Marketing, Purchasing, Human Resources, Shipping, IT, Executive, Public
Relations, Sales, Finance, and Accounting.

columns.name: MANAGER_ID
columns.comment: Manager_id of a department. Foreign key to employee_id column of employees table. The manager_id column of the employee table references this column.

columns.name: LOCATION_ID
columns.comment: Location id where a department is located. Foreign key to location_id column of locations table.

tables.name: EMPLOYEES
tables.comment:
employees table. References with departments,
jobs, job_history tables. Contains a self reference.

columns.name: EMPLOYEE_ID
columns.comment: Primary key of employees table.

columns.name: FIRST_NAME
columns.comment: First name of the employee. A not null column.

columns.name: LAST_NAME
columns.comment: Last name of the employee. A not null column.

columns.name: EMAIL
columns.comment: Email id of the employee

columns.name: PHONE_NUMBER
columns.comment: Phone number of the employee; includes country code and area code

columns.name: HIRE_DATE
columns.comment: Date when the employee started on this job. A not null column.

columns.name: JOB_ID
columns.comment:
Current job of the employee; foreign key to job_id column of the
jobs table. A not null column.

columns.name: SALARY
columns.comment:
Monthly salary of the employee. Must be greater
than zero (enforced by constraint emp_salary_min)

columns.name: COMMISSION_PCT
columns.comment:
Commission percentage of the employee; Only employees in sales
department elgible for commission percentage

columns.name: MANAGER_ID
columns.comment:
Manager id of the employee; has same domain as manager_id in
departments table. Foreign key to employee_id column of employees table.
(useful for reflexive joins and CONNECT BY query)

columns.name: DEPARTMENT_ID
columns.comment:
Department id where employee works; foreign key to department_id
column of the departments table

tables.name: JOBS
tables.comment:
jobs table with job titles and salary ranges.
References with employees and job_history table.

columns.name: JOB_ID
columns.comment: Primary key of jobs table.

columns.name: JOB_TITLE
columns.comment: A not null column that shows job title, e.g. AD_VP, FI_ACCOUNTANT

columns.name: MIN_SALARY
columns.comment: Minimum salary for a job title.

columns.name: MAX_SALARY
columns.comment: Maximum salary for a job title

tables.name: JOB_HISTORY
tables.comment:
Table that stores job history of the employees. If an employee
changes departments within the job or changes jobs within the department,
new rows get inserted into this table with old job information of the
employee. Contains a complex primary key: employee_id+start_date.
References with jobs, employees, and departments tables.

columns.name: EMPLOYEE_ID
columns.comment:
A not null column in the complex primary key employee_id+start_date.
Foreign key to employee_id column of the employee table

columns.name: START_DATE
columns.comment:
A not null column in the complex primary key employee_id+start_date.
Must be less than the end_date of the job_history table. (enforced by
constraint jhist_date_interval)

columns.name: END_DATE
columns.comment:
Last day of the employee in this job role. A not null column. Must be
greater than the start_date of the job_history table.
(enforced by constraint jhist_date_interval)

columns.name: JOB_ID
columns.comment:
Job role in which the employee worked in the past; foreign key to
job_id column in the jobs table. A not null column.

columns.name: DEPARTMENT_ID
columns.comment: Department id in which the employee worked in the past; foreign key to deparment_id column in the departments table

tables.name: LOCATIONS
tables.comment:
Locations table that contains specific address of a specific office,
warehouse, and/or production site of a company. Does not store addresses /
locations of customers. references with the departments and countries tables.

columns.name: LOCATION_ID
columns.comment: Primary key of locations table

columns.name: STREET_ADDRESS
columns.comment:
Street address of an office, warehouse, or production site of a company.
Contains building number and street name

columns.name: POSTAL_CODE
columns.comment:
Postal code of the location of an office, warehouse, or production site
of a company.

columns.name: CITY
columns.comment:
A not null column that shows city where an office, warehouse, or
production site of a company is located.

columns.name: STATE_PROVINCE
columns.comment:
State or Province where an office, warehouse, or production site of a
company is located.

columns.name: COUNTRY_ID
columns.comment:
Country where an office, warehouse, or production site of a company is
located. Foreign key to country_id column of the countries table.

tables.name: REGIONS
tables.comment: Regions table that contains region numbers and names. references with the Countries table.

columns.name: REGION_ID
columns.comment: Primary key of regions table.

columns.name: REGION_NAME
columns.comment: Names of regions. Locations are in the countries of these regions.
